summary: The visible suite now passes (2 passed). The bug was in `solution/util.py`: `_parse_class` read ranges like `a-z` into a `ranges` list correctly, but the `match` function it returned only checked the single-character set and never looked at `ranges`. That's why `[a-z]` didn't match `m`, and why `[!a-c]` treated `a` as "not in the class." I added the range check (`lo <= ch <= hi`) to the matcher, and negation and the `/` exclusion work as before. I also changed one thing the tests didn't ask for, in `solution/core.py`. A code comment there says an unterminated `[` should raise an error, but the code only parsed a segment once matching reached it, so a pattern like `x/[b` against `y/z` returned no error. Every pattern segment is now parsed before matching starts, so it raises `ValueError` as the comment intends. The public `glob_match` API is unchanged.
